issue.title: fix(push): verify payload shape to avoid duplicate client rendering
issue.body:
## Summary
`divine-mobile` is seeing duplicate visible push banners. The likely failure mode is that the payload shape causes both OS-level presentation and app-side local rendering for the same incoming notification.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Related Mobile Work
- divinevideo/divine-mobile#4731

## Scope
- verify the exact FCM/APNS payload combinations currently emitted for likes, comments/replies, follows, and reposts
- confirm whether any current payload shapes can trigger both OS-rendered and app-rendered presentation
- adjust payload behavior if needed so mobile can avoid duplicate rendering cleanly

## Acceptance Criteria
- the payload contract for each notification type is documented and verified
- any payload combinations that trigger duplicate rendering are removed or explicitly coordinated with the mobile-side gate

## Done When
- mobile and push-service agree on a payload contract that does not produce duplicate visible notifications

comment.body:
## Verified: the payload shape causing duplicate iOS rendering

Root-caused from `src/fcm_sender.rs` while fixing the mobile side (divinevideo/divine-mobile#4731, PR divinevideo/divine-mobile#4760). Confirmed for likes, comments/replies, follows, and reposts.

### Mechanism (iOS only)
`build_apns_config` attaches an APNS **`aps.alert`** (title/body) + **`content_available`** + **`mutable_content`** (push-type `Alert`) to *every* push that has a title/body — i.e. all notification types (added in #17). On iOS **background/terminated**:
- the OS presents the `aps.alert` banner (via the app's Notification Service Extension), **and**
- `content_available` wakes the Flutter background isolate, which then built a **second, local** notification → **two banners for one push**.

Android stays data-only (`notification: None`, `android: None`) → the app renders once, no duplicate. iOS **foreground** renders once (mobile does not enable foreground OS-presentation).

### Resolution — no backend change required
Fixed on the client (divinevideo/divine-mobile#4760): FlutterFire surfaces the OS-presented `aps.alert` as `RemoteMessage.notification`, so the background handler now renders a local notification **only for data-only messages** (`message.notification == null`). The OS-presented banner remains tappable and routes via `onMessageOpenedApp` / `getInitialMessage` using the `data` keys.

We deliberately recommend **keeping `aps.alert` server-side**: a silent / data-only iOS push is not reliably delivered when the app is terminated, so the alert is load-bearing for terminated delivery. The client is the correct layer to de-duplicate.

### Documented contract (no change needed)
- **iOS:** `aps.alert` + `content_available` + `mutable_content`; `data` carries the routing fields (`type` lowercase, `eventId`, `referencedEventId`, `senderPubkey`); title/body are filtered out of custom data (already in `aps.alert`).
- **Android:** data-only.
- **Invariant:** one incoming push → one visible banner, with the client owning de-dup via `RemoteMessage.notification`.

If the team would rather the server drive de-dup, the alternative is data-only iOS + an explicit client render — but that trades away reliable terminated delivery, so the client-side gate is the lower-risk fix. Closing the loop for divinevideo/divine-mobile#4731.

issue.title: fix(push): make notification payload targets authoritative for mobile routing and attribution
issue.body:
## Summary
`divine-mobile` still needs notification payloads and upstream notification data to be authoritative enough for correct routing and attribution. Follow notifications, comment/reply targets, and referenced video metadata all need a reliable contract so the client can route safely and avoid wrong-video attribution.

## Assignee
`@dcadenas`

## Related Mobile Work
- divinevideo/divine-mobile#4727
- divinevideo/divine-mobile#4730

## Scope
- verify what fields are currently available in push payloads for each notification type
- document which fields are authoritative for routing and which are presentation-only
- identify and fix any payload/data-integrity gaps that leave mobile unable to distinguish the correct target
- coordinate with upstream notification producers if the inconsistency is not owned directly in `divine-push-service`

## Acceptance Criteria
- the routing/attribution payload contract is explicit
- mobile has authoritative target data or a clearly documented safe fallback contract
- any upstream dependency is linked and tracked

## Done When
- mobile can rely on the payload contract without guessing ownership or target identity

issue.title: chore(deploy): roll out divine-push-service to GKE environments
issue.body:
## Goal

Get divine-push-service running in GKE, starting with poc/staging, then production.

## Prerequisites

- divinevideo/divine-iac-coreconfig#364 must be merged first (Firebase env vars + namespace fix)

## Tasks

### 1. Verify Terraform has been applied

Confirm that `terragrunt apply` has been run for all environments (poc, staging, production):
- GCP service accounts exist (`divine-push-{env}@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com`)
- Secret Manager secrets exist (`divine-push-service-nostr-key-{env}`)
- Cross-project FCM IAM binding is active on `openvine-co`

### 2. Deploy to poc and verify

- Trigger CI to build and push image to poc Artifact Registry
- Verify the service starts, connects to relay, and can send test notifications
- Check health endpoint responds

### 3. Deploy to staging and verify

Same verification as poc.

### 4. Deploy to production

- Merge production image deploy PR in IAC repo
- Monitor logs and health

## Already done

- ~~Upload APNs auth key in Firebase console~~ — APNs certificates already configured in openvine-co (valid until March 2027)
- CI rewrite + ADC support (PR #2 merged)
- IAC CI/CD workflow support (divine-iac-coreconfig#313 merged)

comment.body:
`divine-iac-coreconfig#364` is now closed, so this rollout issue appears unblocked on the infra prerequisite.

Since `@dcadenas` is driving backend notification work, assigning this to him as the backend push DRI.

Suggested closeout path from here:
- confirm Terraform / GKE prereqs are applied in `poc`, `staging`, and `production`
- deploy to `poc` and verify health, relay connectivity, and test push delivery
- deploy to `staging` and repeat verification
- deploy to `production` and monitor logs / health after rollout

Please use this issue thread to check off environment-by-environment rollout status so we have one place to track backend push readiness.

Related mobile-side work that depends on this landing cleanly:
- divinevideo/divine-mobile#4207
- divinevideo/divine-mobile#4387
